correctness.rationale: For all n>=3 and 0<p<1 the stationary symmetric Markov even-spin expansion has strictly positive coefficients and positive definite gap Hessian. Time reversal imposes symmetric unique global optimum. The derivative at all-zero gaps is -(1-(1-p)^j)(1-(1-p)^(n-j))/4; strict central index margin plus convex KKT yields exact short-horizon even/odd grouping. For n=5 the exact reduced derivative is positive factor times rho*u^3+u^2-K(u+1); strictly one positive root and boundary signs yield the unique Tc=2log(2/(1+rho))/gamma and inner-longer-gap classification. The p=1 Jensen case is separate. Standalone 31924 exact/supplementary checks succeeded, finite grids not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: Temporal detection design for intermittent availability exhibits a motivated trade-off between repeat observations of the same state and temporal diversification, demonstrated in Jensen et al. (2022). The new all-n short-time parity law and exact nontrivial n=5 bifurcation specify where clustered replication switches to spread sampling. Exact all-horizon n=5 and independent parameter threshold give a reusable benchmark beyond known n=3/4 cases, without claiming empirical deployment benefits.
